scalesUsed.notes: E - F# - G - A - B - C - D - E
scalesUsed.application: Foundation for all chord progressions and vocal melody throughout the song
Distorted lead guitar lines and power chord riff phrasing in the chorus

keyAndScale.modalCharacter: Aeolian (Natural Minor) with major borrowed chords from the relative major (G major)
keyAndScale.relativeMinor: E minor is the relative minor of G major

mainProgression.description: Haunting verse progression using extended chord voicings that create an atmospheric, melancholy feel. The Cmaj7 and G6 add color to the standard minor key movement.

sectionProgressions.description: Quiet, palm-muted progression creating tension and atmosphere beneath Dolores O'Riordan's restrained vocal delivery
Simplified, powerful open chords with full strumming intensity for the explosive 'In your head' sections
Same chord progression as chorus but with distorted power chord voicings and aggressive strumming

harmonicFunction: Em (i) - Tonic minor chord establishing the dark, brooding home key
Cmaj7 (VImaj7) - Submediant with major seventh adding dreamlike, ethereal color in verses
G6 (III6) - Mediant major chord with added sixth for warmth and movement
D/F# (VII) - Subtonic chord with bass note creating smooth chromatic bass line (F# to G)
C (VI) - Simplified submediant in chorus for powerful, direct harmonic impact
G (III) - Relative major chord providing brightness against the minor tonic
D (VII) - Subtonic chord driving back toward the tonic with strong resolution

techniques.name: Palm-Muted Verse Strumming
techniques.description: Controlled palm muting technique used in the verse sections to create a restrained, percussive quality that contrasts dramatically with the open chorus

notes: Em: 0-2-2-0-0-0 (standard open Em shape)
Cmaj7: X-3-2-0-0-0 (open Cmaj7 voicing)
G6: 3-2-0-0-0-0 (open G6 voicing with open B and high E)
D/F#: 2-0-0-2-3-2 (D chord with F# in the bass)
Rest the palm edge lightly on the strings near the bridge
Adjust palm pressure for varying degrees of mute intensity
Strum downward with a controlled, even motion
sequence: Position palm edge gently on strings just ahead of the bridge saddles
Play Em with moderate palm muting for two bars
Transition to Cmaj7 maintaining consistent mute pressure
Move to G6, keeping the muted tone steady
Finish phrase on D/F# before repeating the cycle
tips: The palm mute should be light enough to hear pitch but heavy enough to dampen sustain
Keep consistent palm pressure throughout the verse for even tone
Practice releasing the mute cleanly when transitioning to the chorus
The contrast between muted verse and open chorus is the key to this song's dynamics

techniques.name: Dynamic Strumming Contrast
techniques.description: Dramatic shift from quiet, palm-muted verse strumming to powerful, open chorus strumming that gives Zombie its signature explosive energy

notes: Verse dynamics: soft, controlled palm-muted strumming (pp to mp)
Chorus dynamics: full-volume open strumming with aggressive attack (f to ff)
The transition should feel sudden and dramatic, not gradual
Use full arm strumming motion in chorus vs. wrist-only in verse
Let all strings ring openly in the chorus for maximum impact
sequence: Play the verse with palm-muted, restrained strumming
On the last beat before the chorus, lift the palm and increase attack
Explode into the chorus with full open strumming
Maintain high energy throughout the chorus section
Return to palm muting when verse resumes
tips: Practice the transition point repeatedly until it feels natural
The dynamic contrast is what makes this song powerful - don't hold back on the chorus
In the chorus, strum through all six strings for full resonance
Use a slightly thicker pick for more aggressive chorus attack
details.progression: Em - C - G - D (open chorus strumming)

techniques.name: Power Chord Chorus Variation
techniques.description: Alternative approach to the chorus using power chords with distortion for a heavier, more aggressive interpretation closer to the studio recording's layered guitars

notes: E5: 0-2-2-X-X-X (open low E with power chord shape)
C5: X-3-5-X-X-X (3rd fret A string root)
G5: 3-5-5-X-X-X (3rd fret low E root)
D5: X-5-7-X-X-X (5th fret A string root)
Use downstrokes exclusively for driving rhythm
Add slight palm muting between chord hits for tightness
sequence: Switch to bridge pickup for brighter distorted tone
Play E5 power chord with aggressive downstrokes
Slide to C5 position with quick transition
Move to G5 on the low E string root
Finish on D5 before cycling back to E5
tips: Keep the fretting hand relaxed to allow quick position changes
Mute unused strings with the underside of the fretting fingers
This technique works great with a second guitarist playing open chords
Dial in moderate gain - too much distortion will sound muddy at this tempo

sections.name: Intro
sections.description: Clean, atmospheric opening with palm-muted arpeggiated chords establishing the song's haunting mood
notes: Begin with light palm muting for a subdued, percussive tone
Let the chord shapes ring slightly under the mute for pitch clarity
Establish the rhythmic feel at 80 BPM before vocals enter
Keep dynamics soft to create space for the later explosive chorus

sections.name: Verse
sections.description: Restrained verse section with controlled palm-muted strumming supporting the quiet, intense vocal delivery
notes: Maintain steady palm-mute pressure throughout the verse
The bass note walk from E to C to G to F# creates a descending bass line
Keep volume low to set up the dynamic contrast with the chorus
Strumming pattern: steady eighth notes with slight accent on beats 1 and 3

sections.name: Chorus
sections.description: Explosive chorus with the iconic the signature vocals backed by open, full-volume strumming
notes: Release all palm muting for open, resonant chord strumming
Full-arm strumming with aggressive downstrokes on each beat
Let all strings ring out for maximum volume and sustain
The shift from muted verse to open chorus should be dramatic and immediate

sections.name: Verse 2
sections.description: Return to restrained verse dynamics with palm-muted strumming, building tension for the second chorus
notes: Return to palm-muted technique after the chorus energy
Slightly more intensity than the first verse to maintain forward momentum
Focus on clean chord transitions under the mute
The extended chord voicings (Cmaj7, G6) add harmonic richness to the quiet section

sections.name: Chorus / Outro
sections.description: Extended final chorus section with increasing intensity, layered guitars, and the signature vocal wail driving the song to its conclusion
notes: Maximum strumming intensity for the final choruses
In the original recording, distorted guitars layer over the clean strumming here
Repeat the chorus progression multiple times with building energy
Song fades out on the repeating Em - C - G - D cycle

guitar.recommended: Fender Stratocaster or similar single-coil guitar
guitar.pickup: Neck or middle pickup for clean verse tones; bridge pickup for distorted chorus sections

amp.recommended: Fender Twin Reverb or similar clean amp

settings.gain: 3-4 (clean for verse, push to 6-7 for chorus with overdrive)

effects.distortion: Light overdrive or distortion pedal for chorus sections (Boss DS-1 or similar)
effects.delay: Short slapback delay for added depth
effects.reverb: Medium hall reverb for atmospheric quality
effects.other: Chorus pedal (optional) for verse shimmer. Switch distortion on/off between verse and chorus.

beginner.focus: Learn the basic open chord shapes and practice transitioning between them
steps: Master the Em, C, G, and D open chord shapes
Practice smooth transitions between the four chorus chords
Learn basic palm-muting technique on the Em chord
Play through the chorus progression with simple downstrokes

intermediate.focus: Master the extended verse chords and dynamic contrast between sections
steps: Learn the Cmaj7, G6, and D/F# voicings used in the verse
Practice palm-muted strumming at 80 BPM with a metronome
Work on the sudden dynamic shift from muted verse to open chorus
Play through the full song structure with correct dynamics

advanced.focus: Add distorted power chord layers and perfect the overall dynamic arc
steps: Learn the power chord chorus variation (E5-C5-G5-D5)
Practice switching between clean and distorted tones mid-song
Add subtle rhythmic variations and accents to the strumming pattern
Perform the complete song with authentic dynamic range and tone switching

commonMistakes: Not enough dynamic contrast between the muted verse and open chorus
Palm muting too heavily in the verse, killing the pitch entirely
Rushing the tempo during the explosive chorus sections
Neglecting the extended chord voicings (Cmaj7, G6) in favor of basic shapes
practiceRoutine: Warm up with palm-muted strumming on Em for 5 minutes, varying pressure
Practice the verse chord sequence (Em-Cmaj7-G6-D/F#) slowly with clean palm muting
Work on the dynamic transition: play 4 bars muted then 4 bars open, repeating
Play through the full song structure at 80 BPM, focusing on dynamics
Record yourself and listen back to evaluate the dynamic contrast
focusAreas: Palm muting consistency and pressure control
Dynamic contrast between verse and chorus
Clean transitions between extended chord voicings
Rhythmic steadiness at the slow 80 BPM tempo
metronomeWork: Start at 60 BPM with palm-muted strumming on single chord
Practice chord changes at 60 BPM, increasing to 80 BPM (song tempo)
Work on the verse progression with metronome clicks on beats 2 and 4
Play full song at tempo, using metronome to prevent rushing during loud chorus
